conditions: Improper integral on the nonnegative real line.
spoken_aliases: the integral from zero to infinity of e to the power of negative x d x equals one
integral from zero to infinity of e raised to the power of open parenthesis negative x close parenthesis with respect to x equals one

evidence: For finite R>0, the antiderivative -exp(-x) gives the integral from zero to R as 1-exp(-R). Take R to positive infinity; exp(-R) tends to zero. This proves convergence and the value one.
Reference cross-check: https://openstax.org/books/calculus-volume-2/pages/3-7-improper-integrals. Checked 2026-11-27. Proposed maintainer approval; not independent human certification.
